title: Exponent left in the denominator after simplifying a power
source: Theory IGCSE-14.7 Quick check 1 (p^2/p^6=1/p^4, so k=4); book Worked example 23(c) style, new numbers
stem: The fraction \((p^{m|int})/(p^{n|int})\) simplifies to \(1/p^k\). What is the value of \(k\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Dividing the powers gives an exponent of {m|int}-{n|int}=-{K|int}, so k={K|int}.
steps.note: K is n minus m. Original: p^2/p^6, k=4.

title: Constant remaining in a cancelled denominator
source: Theory IGCSE-14.7 Quick check 2 ((x^2-4x+3)/(x^2-7x+12)=(x-1)/(x-4), so d=4); book Worked example 23(d) style, new numbers
stem: After cancelling, \((x^2-{B1|int}x+{C1|int})/(x^2-{B2|int}x+{C2|int})=(x-{r|int})/(x-d)\). What is the value of \(d\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The numerator is \((x-{r|int})(x-{s|int})\) and the denominator is \((x-{s|int})(x-{d|int})\). Cancelling \(x-{s|int}\) leaves denominator \(x-{d|int}\), so \(d={d|int}\).

title: Constant in the numerator of a sum of unit fractions
source: Theory IGCSE-14.7 Quick check 3 (1/(x+1)+1/(x+2)=(2x+3)/((x+1)(x+2)), so n=3); book Worked example 26 style, new numbers

title: Write algebraic fractions as a single fraction

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2021), Question 4(e) only, both parts. Official answers and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark. Parts 4(a)–(d) are omitted.

stem:
This question is 0580/43/O/N/21 Question 4(e), taken from the official QP.

Write each of the following as a single fraction, in its simplest form.

(i) \(\dfrac{1}{2a}\div\dfrac{3}{4b}\)  [2]

(ii) \(2-\dfrac{x}{x-1}\)  [2]

steps.name: M
steps.text_tex: For (i), multiplying by the reciprocal gives \(\dfrac{1}{2a}\times\dfrac{4b}{3}=\dfrac{4b}{6a}\).
steps.note: MS 4(e)(i): M1 for (1/(2a)) times (4b/3) or better.

steps.name: B2
steps.note: MS 4(e)(ii): B1 for 2(x-1)-x or equivalent seen.

steps.name: A
steps.note: MS 4(e)(ii): (x-2)/(x-1) final answer, nfww. Independent check: (2x-2-x)/(x-1)=(x-2)/(x-1).
